title: ～まま — “as it is / left as ～”
summary: まま means that a state stays unchanged while another action or situation happens. It attaches to the past or ない form of a verb, or to a noun with の and an adjective in its plain form: 靴を履いたまま, 窓を開けたまま.

patterns.form: 動詞た形・ない形 ＋ まま
patterns.gloss: 履いたまま / つけたまま / 食べないまま

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ の ＋ まま／い形容詞 ＋ まま／な形容詞 ＋ な ＋ まま
patterns.gloss: 昔のまま / 若いまま / 元気なまま

body.p: まま is a noun meaning “the state just as it was.” After a word that expresses a state, it means “with that state left unchanged.” Verbs normally take the past form, which carries a ている sense.
It often describes something done in a way that is not normal, or not allowed: 窓を開けたまま出かけてしまった, テレビをつけたまま寝てしまった. It also appears in prohibitions such as 靴を履いたまま入らないでください.
The following action happens at the same time as the unchanged state, so a contradictory action cannot follow, such as 座ったまま立つ.

examples.ja: 靴（くつ）を履（は）いたまま入（はい）らないでください。
examples.romaji: Kutsu o haita mama hairanai de kudasai.
examples.tr: Please don't come in with your shoes on.

examples.ja: 窓（まど）を開（あ）けたまま、出（で）かけてしまった。
examples.romaji: Mado o aketa mama, dekakete shimatta.
examples.tr: I went out with the window left open.

examples.ja: テレビをつけたまま、寝（ね）てしまった。
examples.romaji: Terebi o tsuketa mama, nete shimatta.
examples.tr: I fell asleep with the TV left on.

pitfalls: Use the past form of the verb: 履いたまま, not 履くまま or 履いているまま.
Nouns take の and na-adjectives take な: 昔のまま, 元気なまま.
